probe_page: frontend/src/probe.tsx built to web/dist/probe.html (development entry, not a product surface)
question: do the components the overhaul wants need style-src-attr unsafe-inline?
method: the page measures the computed style of one element per library and reports it; a blocked inline style is ignored by the engine while its attribute stays in the DOM, so the computed value is the honest signal. The strict policy was captured with Chrome --dump-dom; the proposed policy with the page own POST.
conclusion: No CSP change is needed: all three components were position-, transform- and virtualisation-correct under the strict policy the workspace already uses, because React writes styles through the CSSOM at runtime, which CSP does not police. The risk that would need style-src-attr is markup-level style attributes and injected <style> elements, and both stay out: the built HTML carries no style attribute (checked in live-r0.json) and runtime CSS-in-JS libraries are excluded by docs/87.

runner.note: headless Chrome one-shot invocations are flaky in this sandbox: one dump-dom completed and the page POST completed; the script records which channel produced each variant rather than hiding the difference.

limits: One Chrome build, one machine, one build of the app.
The probe does not exercise every component in the chosen libraries, only one representative each.
